findings.message: The public host-function signature types `ctx.hostContext` as optional and possibly undefined, but the runtime always sets it. Extension authors have to cast or null-check to use the new bag, which works against the 'defaults to {}' guarantee. `CallableFn` receives `ctx: RuntimeContextLike`, which declares `readonly hostContext?: Record<string, unknown> | undefined`, while `RuntimeContext` declares `readonly hostContext: Record<string, unknown>` (types/runtime.ts:174). Every new test has to write `(ctx as RuntimeContext).hostContext` to reach it without a null check (host-context.test.ts lines 55, 85, 113, 138, 170).

`CallableFn` gives host functions a `ctx` of type `RuntimeContextLike`, and there `hostContext` is optional (`Record<string, unknown> | undefined`). The runtime always sets it to an object, but extension authors can't see that from the type. They have to cast to `RuntimeContext`, as every new test does with `(ctx as RuntimeContext).hostContext`, or add pointless `?.` checks. That undercuts the stated goal of letting extensions use this bag at call time. Make it non-optional here (`readonly hostContext: Record<string, unknown>`) to match `RuntimeContext`. `CallableFn` gives host functions a `ctx` of type `RuntimeContextLike`, and there `hostContext` is optional (`Record<string, unknown> | undefined`). The host integration docs describe `ctx.metadata` for host functions but never mention the new `hostContext` option or field, so hosts and extension authors have no documentation for the feature. A grep for `hostContext` under docs/ returns nothing. integration-host.md:257-288 lists the `ctx` contents as 'variables, pipeValue, and session metadata' and documents only `ctx.metadata`. The change edits only CHANGELOG.md and source files.

The host integration docs cover `ctx.metadata` for host functions, but there is nothing about the new `hostContext` option or `ctx.hostContext`. They also don't explain how it differs from `metadata` (it holds any value type, always defaults to `{}`, and is shared by reference). Without that, the feature only shows up in the CHANGELOG. Adding `hostContext` as a required member of the exported `RuntimeContext` interface breaks type-checking for any downstream code that builds a `RuntimeContext` object literal. The CHANGELOG lists the change only under 'Added'. `readonly hostContext: Record<string, unknown>;` has no `?`, unlike the neighbouring `metadata?`. Inside this repo, the only literal builder, `assertType`'s `minimalContext` (eval/index.ts:89-119), had to be patched to add `hostContext: {}`. `RuntimeContext` is exported from '@rcrsr/rill', as the test import shows.

`RuntimeContext` is a public exported interface, and this adds a required field to it. Any downstream code that builds a `RuntimeContext` object literal (test mocks, custom harnesses) will stop compiling. Note this in the CHANGELOG, or consider whether it should be optional on the public type the way `metadata` is. `RuntimeContext` is a public exported interface, and this adds a required field to it. The host's `hostContext` object is passed by reference and is not frozen, so any extension or host function can add, replace or delete entries. Those changes are seen by every other extension in the run and by the host's original object. The change does not document this sharing. `hostContext: options.hostContext ?? {}` stores the caller's object as-is, and `createChildContext` copies the same reference (`hostContext: parent.hostContext`). The test 'child context shares same hostContext reference as parent' asserts `refs[0]` is `sharedContext`. The type is `Record<string, unknown>`; the `readonly` applies only to the property, not to the object's contents.

The context stores the host's object by reference with no copy or freeze, and every child context shares that same reference. Any extension or host function can mutate it, and the change is visible to all later calls in the run. If the host reuses the same options object across `execute()` calls, the changes also carry over into other runs and sessions. If shared mutable state isn't intended, freeze or shallow-copy the object. Either way, document the sharing semantics. The 'child context propagation' test runs a conditional branch, which may not actually create a child context through `createChildContext`. It never checks propagation into closures or other scopes that do create child contexts, such as closure invocation or loop bodies. Add a test that calls the host function from inside a closure body or a loop, so the `createChildContext` path is really covered.
